identitySignals: The agenda names the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE), a California state agency; Wikipedia describes CAL FIRE as the state fire department under the California Natural Resources Agency

The California Grants Portal lists the FY22-23 Urban and Community Forestry Green Schoolyards grant as administered by the Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE), matching OUSD's 'Oakland Living Schoolyards Implementation Project' grant award
OUSD's own Living Schoolyards Partners page says OUSD was awarded CalFire grants for 2 implementation sites and 14 planning sites in 2024
research.notes: Public state agency. The official site fire.ca.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so website, phone, email and address were left null rather than uncited. Phone and email on the grants portal are specific to the urban forestry grant program, not the agency's main line.

profile.legalName: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
profile.summary: CAL FIRE is a California state agency. It provides fire protection in areas of the state under state responsibility and manages the state's private and public forests. It also runs grant programs, including urban and community forestry grants for green schoolyards.

sources.title: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Wikipedia
FY22-23 Urban and Community Forestry Green Schoolyards - California Grants Portal
Living Schoolyards Partners - Oakland Unified School District

review.notes: CAL FIRE is the state agency that administers the Urban and Community Forestry Green Schoolyards grant (grants.ca.gov), and OUSD's own page confirms its 2024 CalFire awards, matching the agenda's grant items. Legal name, org type and the neutral summary are supported by Wikipedia and the grants portal; all contact fields are null.
